01 — Foundation

Brand & Logo

Flagright should feel composed, precise, and enterprise-ready. The brand carries high-stakes compliance with calm control, not visual noise.

Brand intro

Calm technology that moves fast.

Flagright represents the operating layer behind financial crime compliance. Every brand expression should feel controlled, technically credible, and quietly powerful.

01

Show composure inside complexity.

02

Let product UI and proof lead the story.

03

Use cinematic depth with restraint.

Logo assets
Dark BG
White logo only · Use on #1C1C1D and #252628
Use the white logo on primary dark surfaces. Do not use this variation on light backgrounds.
Light BG
Colored logo only · Use on #FFFFFF and #E1E3E5
Mark #1169F9 · Wordmark #293F7A. Keep the original SVG colors intact.
Logo usage rules
Do

Use the white SVG lockup on dark brand surfaces such as #1C1C1D and #252628.

Do

Use the colored SVG lockup on white backgrounds and light print applications.

No

Do not place the colored logo on dark backgrounds. It loses contrast and brand clarity.

No

Do not place the white logo on white or soft-light backgrounds. Use the colored version instead.

No

Do not stretch, recolor, rotate, or rebuild the mark or wordmark as text.

Logo clear space

Use half the logo symbol as clear space

Keep a clear space of Y/2 around the full lockup, where Y is the height of the Flagright symbol. No text, borders, UI, or imagery should enter this area.

Minimum digital size: keep the full lockup at 120 px wide or larger. Use the symbol alone only for compact product, favicon, or avatar placements.

Logo with secondary line

Use this lockup when the logo needs added context, such as event banners, booth graphics, covers, and speaking backdrops.

Use the light-background version for print materials or light surfaces. Keep the layout calm, centred, and highly legible.

01B — Foundation

Design Principles

Flagright should feel calm, controlled, and technically credible. Every page should help people understand a complex system without adding more complexity.

Visual direction rules
Calm, cinematic imagery

Use scenery as atmosphere, not decoration. The frame should feel quiet, expansive, and premium so the product and message can lead.

DO

Deep blue and neutral dominance with small warm light accents.

DO

Wide horizons, dusk skies, reflective water, mist, or low-light depth.

NO

No stock office scenes, loud AI tropes, neon gradients, or lifestyle humans.

Light grid structure

The grid gives infinite scenery a boundary. It should suggest regulatory structure, system architecture, and control without becoming heavy.

DO

Use fine 1px lines, modular frames, and clean section breaks.

DO

Let grids organize product UI, proof points, and content groups.

NO

Do not overuse grids as decoration or fill every empty space with lines.

Clean, structured layouts

Every section should be easy to consume. Use hierarchy, spacing, and restrained copy to make product depth feel simple and decisive.

DO

Use clear content blocks, generous breathing room, and direct labels.

DO

Prioritize product UI, verified metrics, and one strong message per section.

NO

Do not stack too many visual styles, long paragraphs, or competing focal points.

03 — Foundation

Typography

Lora brings calm authority. DM Sans keeps the system clear and readable. Space Mono gives data, labels, and metrics a technical edge.

Typeface role
Lora

Lora represents calmness, credibility, and institutional authority

Use Lora for primary headings, section titles, premium editorial statements, and hero messaging that should feel calm and assured.

DM Sans

DM Sans keeps information easy to consume

Use DM Sans for body copy, UI descriptions, helper text, supporting paragraphs, and any copy that needs fast readability.

Space Mono

Space Mono signals data and system logic

Use Space Mono for labels, tabs, badges, data values, IDs, timestamps, and numbers that should feel technical and precise.

Heading system
Lora / Display · 48–72px · italic emphasis only
Calm technology that moves fast
Lora / Display on light · same-color emphasis
Compliance infrastructure built for scale
Lora / Headline on dark · color emphasis
The AI operating system for financial crime compliance
Lora / Headline on light · color emphasis
Move from manual review to AI-native decisions
Lora / Title · 24–32px · no highlight
The AI operating system for financial crime compliance
Lora / Title on light · no highlight
Built for compliance teams that move fast
Rules
CaseUse sentence case for all headings and UI copy. Space Mono labels, tabs, badges, and eyebrows can stay all caps.
LabelsAll type-spec labels use Space Mono in uppercase. Keep them functional, short, and technical.
WeightUse Lora Medium on dark backgrounds. Use Lora SemiBold on light backgrounds to hold contrast.
PunctuationHeadings should not end with a full stop unless the sentence needs it grammatically.
Dark modeUse #A9AEC5 for the sentence and #FFFFFF for the key phrase. No italics for headline emphasis.
Light modeUse #585D76 for the sentence and #131313 for the key phrase. Keep the contrast strong.
DisplayUse italics only in the largest hero-level display style. The full display heading stays in one color.
Body and data
DM Sans / Body copy · 14–16px · weight 300

Use DM Sans for all body copy. It should explain capability, process, and benefits with clarity and speed.

DM Sans / Supporting copy on light · #585D76

Use it for supporting paragraphs, captions, and helper text on light backgrounds while keeping contrast readable.

Space Mono / Numbers and metrics · regular

05 — Foundation

Scenery Rules

Scenery should create calm, scale, and emotional space. It supports the product story; it should never become the product story.

How to frame scenes

Keep the scene wide

Use panoramic compositions, long horizons, large sky fields, clouds, and open negative space. Avoid tight crops or busy foregrounds.

Keep the palette restrained

Let deep blue and dark neutrals dominate. Add only a small amount of warm light for cinematic depth.

Keep the grid light

Grid lines bring structure to infinite scenery. Use them as a thin, low-opacity frame, not as a heavy pattern.

Scenery gallery
Open sky and transformation
Reflective water
Minimal mountain silhouette
Open sky and transformation
Reflective water
Minimal mountain silhouette
Use and avoid

Use

  • — Dusk, dawn, low-light skies, mist, clouds, water, glass, quiet city scale
  • — Minimal scenes where product UI or message can sit clearly
  • — Rare cinematic metaphors when a page needs scale or transformation

Avoid

  • — Corporate stock photography, handshakes, office teams, smiling lifestyle scenes
  • — Bright daylight, green sustainability cues, neon AI effects, cyberpunk visuals
  • — Overusing scenery in every section; use it only where emotion or scale is needed
06 — Components

Buttons & CTAs

CTAs should be direct and minimal. Primary buttons carry the main action. Secondary CTAs behave like text links, without a box.

Primary CTA
Use for the main conversion action · two sizes only

The arrow is part of the CTA behavior. On hover, the arrow moves slightly upward and to the right to suggest forward motion.

Secondary CTA
Use for supporting actions · no rectangle

Secondary CTAs should stay quiet. Use text plus arrow only; do not place a border or filled background around it.

07 — Components

Badges & Status

Badges should feel like system labels. Use Space Mono, all caps, tight padding, and semantic color only when the state needs meaning.

Badge variations

With status dot

Use when the badge communicates live state, risk, or process status.

Cleared Review Escalated AI Resolved

With icon

Use simple icons only when they improve recognition. Avoid mixing too many icons in one area.

↗ Exported ✦ AI Agent ⚠ Needs QA ✓ Filed

08 — Components

Cards & Metrics

Metric cards should be quiet and confident. The number carries the weight; the label explains the operational outcome.

Metric card rule
93%
False positive reduction
10x
Faster alert investigations
18min
Average SAR drafting time
10x
Faster regulatory impact assessment

Use Space Mono regular for the number. Keep labels around 15px, bottom aligned, and clearly secondary to the number.

09 — Components

Data Tables

Tables should feel structured without becoming heavy. Use horizontal lines for separation and avoid vertical grid lines unless the data truly requires it.

Table rules
Use horizontal rhythmRows should be separated by horizontal strokes. Keep columns clean and easy to scan.
Avoid vertical clutterDo not add vertical lines by default. Use spacing, alignment, and typography to separate columns.

10 — Components

Navigation

Navigation should help people understand where they are and what layer they are exploring. Use top navigation for horizontal choices and vertical navigation for longer content groups.

Top aligned navigation

Platform overview

Use this pattern for product sections where all options sit at the same level. The active state is a thin blue underline.

Investigations

Use short labels and keep the interaction direct. Avoid long tab names that slow scanning.

Risk scoring

Tabs work best when each option changes a focused content area below the navigation.

Governance

Keep tab states calm: blue for active, muted grey for inactive, no loud hover effects.

Vertical aligned navigation

FCC coverage from onboarding to ongoing monitoring

Use this layout when the section is longer and needs a persistent index.

Scale investigations without adding operational drag

Vertical navigation gives the reader a map while keeping the main content focused.

Configure workflows without engineering dependency

Keep items short, mono, and separated by horizontal rules.

Support coverage that stays close to the customer

Use vertical navigation when the story has clear stages or pillars.
